findings.title: Update invalidation compares an organization-aware model against the raw updated model
findings.body: update() obtains the original model through getById() (line 91), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false whenever the linked organization is disabled. The JPA-backed getForLogin result, however, is based on the stored enabled/hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC fields and does not exclude IdPs merely because their organization is disabled. Therefore, for an IdP in a disabled organization that currently qualifies in the stored data, changing hideOnLogin or linkOnly to a disqualifying value makes both the wrapped original and the updated model fail getLoginPredicate(), so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() returns without invalidating any login cache. The stale cached ID remains and can reappear when the organization is re-enabled, even though the IdP is now hidden or link-only. The comparison should use the unwrapped stored model/fields rather than the organization-aware isEnabled() view.

findings.title: Empty-string organizationId collides with the null organization cache key
findings.body: getForLogin() uses "" as the IdentityProviderListQuery search key when organizationId is null, while a caller-supplied organizationId of "" is also non-null and is kept as "". Under the IdentityProviderStorageProvider contract these are different requests: null means IdPs from any organization, whereas "" is passed through as a specific organization-id search. The cache therefore conflates the two cases, so getForLogin(ORG_ONLY or ALL, "") can return the cached all-organizations result, or the reverse ordering can make a null-organization request reuse an empty/specific-organization result. Use a distinct sentinel that cannot be a supplied organizationId, or include the organizationId in the cache key.

findings.title: New cache test cleans up a literal "alias" IdP instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: The cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, which binds a resource for an IdP literally named "alias" rather than each created idp-alias-i provider; the same mistake is repeated for idp-alias-20 at line 425. Cleanup will attempt to delete a non-existent provider and leave the twenty-plus created IdPs in the shared test realm, making the test order-dependent and potentially polluting other tests in the class. Capture each created alias in a lambda that deletes that alias.

findings.title: Login-cache test never creates or removes a login-qualified IdP
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates a hideOnLogin IdP and removes a disabled IdP to assert that non-qualifying operations do not invalidate the caches, and it exercises invalidation only through an update that changes login availability. It never creates an enabled login-qualified IdP, nor removes one, after the login caches are populated, so a regression in the new positive invalidation paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create() and remove() would not be caught. Add cases asserting that both operations clear the REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches and that subsequent getForLogin calls return the updated membership.
